title: I wonder where she lives
goal: Put questions inside sentences, ask whether something is true, and use whole clauses as subjects.

intro.text: Inside a sentence, a question keeps its question word and loses *mI*: *Nerede oturduğunu bilmiyorum*. **Whether** is the verb and its negative: *gelip gelmeyeceğini*. A clause can also be the subject, with no case: *Gelmen önemli*, *Kimin kazanacağı belli değil*.

vocab.en: to be understood; to become clear, to turn out

exercises.question: How do you say **I don't know where she lives**?

why.1: Inside a sentence, *mI* disappears and the verb becomes a noun: *oturduğunu*.
why.2: `-mA` is for actions someone wants; where she lives is a fact, so `-DIk`.

exercises.explain: The question word stays, the verb takes `-DIk` + possessive + accusative: *Nerede otur-duğ-u-n-u bilmiyorum*.

exercises.en: I asked what time the meeting would start.

reject.why: Inside a sentence the question becomes a noun: *başlayacağını*, with the possessive and the accusative.
The meeting is still to come: use `-(y)AcAk`, *başlayacağını*.

exercises.hint: Future, the third-person possessive, then the accusative for *sordum*.
exercises.explain: *başla-y-acağ-ı-n-ı sordum*: **I asked when it would start**.

exercises.label: *gelmek* + *sordu*: she asked whether I would come, whether you would come…
exercises.explain: *Gelip* never changes; the second verb carries the negative, the future, the person and the case: *gel-me-y-eceğ-im-i*.

exercises.prompt: I don't know what to do.

reject.why: You may hear it in speech with a pause, but as a clause it needs the accusative: *ne yapacağımı bilmiyorum*.
*Yapacağını* is what **you** (or he) will do. For **I**, *yapacağımı*.

exercises.explain: `-(y)AcAk` with the possessive of the person who would act: *ne yap-acağ-ım-ı*, **what I'm going to do**.

accept: We still do not know who won.
We still do not know who has won.
We do not know who [won|has won] yet.
We do not yet know who [won|has won].

exercises.en: I asked whether she was at home.

exercises.question: Which sentence means **It's important that you come**?

why.1: The clause is the subject of *önemli*, so it takes no accusative.
why.2: A subject takes no case, and an event that matters takes `-mA`: *gelmen*.

exercises.explain: *Gel-me-n önemli*: the clause is the subject, with no case ending.

exercises.prompt: Is it true that you're moving?

reject.why: The clause is the subject of *doğru*, so no accusative: *taşınacağın*, or *taşınacağınız*.
*Doğru* asks whether a fact is true, so `-DIk`: *taşınacağın*.

exercises.explain: *Taşın-acağ-ınız doğru mu?*: a fact judged true or false takes `-DIk`, and a subject takes no case.

reject.why: As the subject, the question becomes a noun: *dediği*, or *söylediği*.
The clause is the subject of *önemli değil*, so no accusative: *dediği*.

exercises.hint: The subject of *önemli değil*: `-DIk` + possessive, and no case.
exercises.explain: *Ne de-diğ-i önemli değil*: an embedded question as the subject, with no case ending.

exercises.text: It was announced that the meeting had been cancelled.
accept: It was announced that the meeting had been canceled.
It was announced the meeting had been cancelled.

exercises.en: It turned out that Ali was right.

exercises.prompt: Bu raporu yarına kadar bitirmemiz imkânsız.
accept: It is impossible for us to finish this report by tomorrow.
It is impossible for us to finish the report by tomorrow.
It is impossible to finish [this|the] report by tomorrow.
We cannot possibly finish [this|the] report by tomorrow.
There is no way (that) we can finish [this|the] report by tomorrow.

reject.why: The clause is the subject of *normal*: no accusative, *yorgun olman*.

exercises.explain: *Normal* weighs the event, so `-mA`: *yorgun ol-ma-n normal*.

exercises.task: A friend asks about your new neighbour, whom you hardly know. Write three sentences about what you don't know or wonder, with embedded questions (*nerede, ne zaman, kiminle*…) and one **whether** with `-(y)Ip … -mAdIğI`.
models: Yeni komşunun adının ne olduğunu bilmiyorum. Nerede çalıştığını ve ne zaman taşındığını da bilmiyorum. Evli olup olmadığını merak ediyorum.
Yeni komşumuzun nereli olduğunu bilmiyorum. Kiminle yaşadığını hiç sormadım. Çocuğu olup olmadığını yarın kapıcıya soracağım.
checklist: The question word stays: *nerede çalıştığını*, *ne zaman taşındığını*
The verb takes `-DIk` or `-(y)AcAk`, a possessive and a case, and *mI* disappears
A noun doer in the genitive: *komşunun*
